title: A Better Balance
content:
Sofia had always been a hardworking person. She usually woke up early, worked all day, and spent her evenings answering messages or finishing tasks. She believed that being busy meant being productive.

However, after several months of this routine, she began to feel exhausted.

One morning, her friend Laura noticed that something was wrong.

— You don't look well. Are you sleeping enough?

— Not really. I've been working late almost every night.

— And when was the last time you did something just for yourself?

Sofia thought for a moment.

— I honestly don't remember.

Laura smiled.

— Then maybe you need to take better care of yourself.

At first, Sofia thought that improving her well-being would require major changes. She imagined joining an expensive gym, following a strict diet, and completely changing her daily routine.

Instead, she decided to start with small habits.

The next morning, she went for a short walk before work. She didn't exercise for a long time, but she enjoyed being outside and getting some fresh air.

During her lunch break, she stopped working and ate her meal without looking at her phone.

In the evening, she turned off her computer earlier than usual.

— I'm going to try to sleep earlier tonight — she told herself.

After a few weeks, Sofia began to notice a difference. She had more energy during the day and found it easier to concentrate at work. She was also spending more time with her family and friends.

One Saturday, Laura invited her to a park.

— Do you still feel stressed all the time? — Laura asked.

— Much less. I didn't realize how much my routine was affecting me.

— What has helped you the most?

Sofia thought about it.

— Learning that well-being isn't just about exercising or eating healthy food. I also need to rest, spend time with people I love, and give myself a break.

Laura nodded.

— That's a much healthier way of looking at it.

Sofia smiled as they continued walking through the park.

She realized that taking care of her well-being didn't mean having a perfect routine. It meant paying attention to what her body and mind needed.

From then on, she continued working hard, but she stopped believing that she had to be busy all the time.

She learned that sometimes doing less can actually help us live better.
